MAIN THREAD IS NOT BLOCKED: 262 IPC round-trips sampled every 40 ms during the first 12 s show max rtt 15 ms, 0 above 40 ms. The cost is CPU/IO contention in child processes plus late data, not a stalled event loop.

STEADY STATE (the "janky all over the place" complaint): one `touch README.md` on the restored repo produced THREE consecutive full refreshes at +126 ms, +3,972 ms and +7,740 ms, each with a 3,386-3,463 ms ignored walk = 11.3 s of continuously saturated core and 9 git spawns for one file save. Root cause of the repeat: plain `git status` rewrites .git/index (verified: index mtime moved after a touch+status, and did NOT move with `--no-optional-locks`), and src/main/repositoryWatcher.ts:39 explicitly admits `.git/index`, so each refresh schedules the next.

RAYCAST Cmd+H / horus:// COLD LAUNCH: 310 git processes. The restore's 7,080 ms ignored walk runs concurrently with 307 `git remote -v` spawns spanning 520-3,961 ms, because findPullRequestRoot runs three times independently (main's warmupPullRequest, the renderer's previewPullRequestFolder effect, and the renderer's resolvePullRequestRepository) with no shared cache; 103 candidate roots x 3 scans. Under that contention each `git remote -v` costs 96-192 ms instead of ~30 ms.

BACKGROUND: merely copying any GitHub PR URL to the clipboard, with Horus idle in the background and unfocused, spawns 103 `git remote -v` processes over 1.3 s (measured: 3 spawns before the copy, 106 after).

findings.title: `ls-files --others --ignored` with 54 exclusion pathspecs makes every refresh 3.4-7.1 s (regression introduced by e18053e)
findings.line: 1341-1355 (the Promise.all in refresh()); pathspecs built at 323-326
findings.mechanism: refresh() runs three git spawns in one Promise.all, so the snapshot waits for the slowest. The third is `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z -- . :(exclude,glob)<27 dirs>/** :(exclude,glob)**/<27 dirs>/**`. A `:(exclude)` pathspec is an OUTPUT filter, not a traversal pruner: git still opens and reads every directory in the working tree, evaluates .gitignore for all 369,122 ignored files in materialsx-core-3, and only then drops 368,717 of them. Result: 405 paths for 1.9 s of user CPU and 1.5 s of sys CPU. Before e18053e (`git show e18053e -- src/main/repository.ts`, hunk at the old line 136) refresh() was `const [trackedResult, statusResult] = await Promise.all([...])` with no ignored call, i.e. ~60 ms. This single commit is why launch, folder-open and every watcher tick regressed.
findings.evidence: Standalone on ~/Developer/materialx/materialsx-core-3: `real 3.29 / 3.37 / 3.39 / 3.50 s, user 1.85-1.88, sys 1.43-1.60` -> 405 paths. Spawned by the installed Horus during a cold launch, captured with a PATH `git` shim: 6,583 ms and 7,080 ms on two runs; 3,463 ms on a post-startup watcher tick. materialsx-core-4: 6,572-6,813 ms -> 213 paths. Meanwhile `ls-files --cached` = 0.01 s and `status --porcelain=v2` = 0.03-0.06 s. `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z` with NO pathspecs = 1.96 s / 369,122 paths, proving the pathspecs cost MORE than they save (3.4 s vs 2.0 s) because pathspec matching runs per candidate path.
findings.fix: Two-phase listing. Phase 1: `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory --no-empty-directory -z` (measured 0.03-0.04 s; returns 134 entries = 91 collapsed dirs + 43 files, because --directory stops git descending into an ignored directory). Phase 2: drop every entry whose path contains an EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES segment (81 of 91 dirs vanish), then expand the ~12 survivors with a plain recursive readdirSync/opendir walk — no gitignore evaluation is needed because everything under an ignored directory is ignored by definition. During the walk skip directory names in EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_SET, skip `.git`, and when a child directory itself contains `.git` push `<dir>/` and stop descending (git's --others stops at a nested repository boundary). Filter EXCLUDED_IGNORED_EXTENSIONS as today. Keep the existing MAX cap. Verified BYTE-IDENTICAL output on four repositories: materialsx-core-3 405==405 in 44 ms (143x), materialsx-core-4 213==213 in 44 ms (151x), better-code-diff 576==576 in 20 ms (21x), imux 4,207==4,207 in 79 ms — zero only-in-current, zero only-in-new in every case. Working script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fuadnafiz98-Developer-vibes-better-code-diff/2a975ab1-5c84-43b9-bac1-d2fcb5d3d267/scratchpad/reports/tmp/mainstartup/verify3.mjs. A pure-git two-phase (expanding survivors with another `git ls-files -- <dirs>`) is only 1.9x and is NOT recommended. Secondary hardening: move the ignored listing out of the Promise.all so branch/head/statuses/tracked paths publish in ~60 ms and the ignored set merges in a second publish; give it an AbortSignal + hard timeout so a pathological tree can never hold a snapshot.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 3,400-7,000 ms off restoreSettled, off every folder-open, and off every watcher tick

findings.title: Each refresh re-arms the watcher: `git status` rewrites .git/index, which the recursive watch admits, so one file save costs three refreshes / 11.3 s
findings.line: 39 (normalizeChangedPath admits `.git/index`); triggered by the status spawn at src/main/repository.ts:1343
findings.mechanism: normalizeChangedPath returns `.git/index` as a real change (line 39: `return path === '.git/HEAD' || path === '.git/index' || path.startsWith('.git/refs/')`). Plain `git status` performs an optional index refresh and rewrites .git/index whenever stat data is racy — which it is immediately after a save. The recursive fs.watch on the repo root therefore sees Horus's own status call as an external change, schedules another #flush, and runs refresh() again. With refresh at 60 ms this was invisible; with MAIN-1 making refresh 3.4 s the chain is 11 seconds of a pinned core per user save. This is the mechanical explanation for 'janky and slow all over the place'.
findings.evidence: With the installed app open on materialsx-core-3 and settled (3 git spawns total in the preceding 12 s idle), a single `touch README.md` produced 9 git spawns and THREE full refreshes: ignored walks starting at +126 ms (3,463 ms), +3,972 ms (3,386 ms) and +7,740 ms (3,412 ms). Index-write proof: `stat -f %Sm .git/index` = 10:10:56 before; after `touch README.md; git status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z --untracked-files=all` it is 10:18:31; after a second `touch README.md; git --no-optional-locks status ...` it is STILL 10:18:31.
findings.fix: (a) Add `--no-optional-locks` to the status spawn at src/main/repository.ts:1343: `this.#git(['--no-optional-locks','status','--porcelain=v2','--branch','-z','--untracked-files=all'])`. It is a top-level git option and must precede the subcommand. Verified above to stop the index write with identical output. Alternatively set `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` in the env of every spawn in runCommand (src/main/gitCommands.ts:255). (b) Belt and braces: extend the existing self-write suppression to git metadata — have RepositoryService call the watcher's `expectSelfWrite('.git/index')` (src/main/repositoryWatcher.ts:186 already implements the 1 s window) around each refresh, so any index write within ~1 s of the app's own git call is dropped. Do NOT simply stop watching `.git/index`: a `git commit` from a terminal is a real event the app must see.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~7,000 ms of redundant background git work per file save (2 of the 3 refresh cycles); after MAIN-1 it is ~250 ms, but the fix keeps the loop from returning if any future refresh gets slow again
findings.regressionCommit: pre-existing (normalizeChangedPath) but only became expensive with e18053e

findings.title: Raycast Cmd+H / horus:// runs the pull-request root scan THREE times: 307 `git remote -v` spawns on top of a 7 s ignored walk
findings.mechanism: findPullRequestRoot builds its remotes cache inside findMatchingPullRequestRoot (src/main/pullRequestRoots.ts:17-23), so the cache is per-invocation and dies with the call. A horus:// open triggers three independent invocations: (1) main's applyExternalReview -> warmupPullRequest -> findPullRequestRoot (index.ts:166); (2) the renderer's openExternalPullRequest -> openPullRequestFromLocator -> updateNewWorldLocator, whose effect at src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:159 calls previewPullRequestFolder -> findPullRequestRoot; (3) the same handler's resolvePullRequestRepository (src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:504) -> findPullRequestRoot. Each scans 103 candidate roots at concurrency 8 (pullRequestRoots.ts:14, 53-66), each root costing a `stat` plus a `git remote -v` spawn (index.ts:505-511). There is no in-flight dedupe on the URL and no process-level remotes memo. All three run while the restore's ignored walk pins a core, so per-spawn cost inflates from ~30 ms to 96-192 ms.
findings.evidence: PATH-shim trace of `Horus "horus://review?url=https://github.com/nonexistent-org-xyz/nonexistent-repo-xyz/pull/1"` from cold: 310 git spawns total. 307 are `remote -v`, spanning 520 ms to 3,961 ms after process start; individual roots (e.g. ~/Developer/materialx/materialsx-core-4, ~/Developer/andrim) appear three times each. Concurrently, `ls-files --others --ignored` on materialsx-core-3 ran 344 ms -> 7,424 ms. Idle-machine control: the same 103 roots at concurrency 8 take 388 ms total (13 waves, avg 30 ms, max 32 ms).
findings.fix: Three changes in src/main/index.ts. (1) Hoist the remotes cache to module scope: `const remotesByRoot = new Map<string, {at: number; value: Promise<readonly GitRemote[]>}>()` keyed by root with a ~60 s TTL, invalidated when a repository session for that root opens or closes, and have remotesForRoot (index.ts:505) read through it — `git remote -v` output changes about once a month. (2) Dedupe findPullRequestRoot per URL: `const rootFlights = new Map<string, Promise<string|null>>()` so concurrent callers share one scan, plus a resolved-root memo keyed by URL for the life of the process. (3) Have the renderer stop asking at all for the horus:// case: applyExternalReview already knows the root it warmed, so send it with the openExternalPullRequest IPC payload and let useGitWorkflow.ts:504 pass it as preferredRoot, which skips findPullRequestRoot entirely (index.ts:576-579). Also skip the preview effect (useGitWorkflow.ts:153-172) when a preferredRoot is already known.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~2,600 ms and ~205 wasted git process spawns off the Cmd+H path (two of the three scans), and removes the CPU contention that inflates the surviving scan by 3-6x

findings.title: Clipboard polling turns copying any GitHub PR URL into 103 git spawns (plus a full repo open + GitHub fetch on a match) with the app in the background
findings.mechanism: startClipboardWarmup reads the clipboard every 800 ms forever (CLIPBOARD_WARMUP_MS, index.ts:71) and on any change calls warmupPullRequest for any GitHub PR URL it finds. warmupPullRequest -> findPullRequestRoot walks ~/Developer and spawns `git remote -v` across up to 400 candidate roots, and on a match calls openRepository (a full 3.4-7 s ignored refresh, MAIN-1) and then getPullRequestReview (gh CLI + network). The user's own workflow is copying PR URLs, so this fires constantly, including while the Horus window is not focused. WARMUP_COOLDOWN_MS (index.ts:72) only dedupes the same URL for 60 s; a different PR pays the full price again.
findings.evidence: Installed app left idle in the background on materialsx-core-3 (3 git spawns in the preceding 12 s). `printf 'https://github.com/nonexistent-org-xyz/nonexistent-repo-xyz/pull/7' | pbcopy` produced 103 further `git remote -v` spawns spanning 322-1,664 ms after the copy (gitcalls.log went from 3 to 106 lines). The slug matched nothing, so this is the CHEAP case — a matching slug additionally opens the repository and runs the 3.4-7 s ignored walk.
findings.fix: Gate the warmup on cheap pre-checks before any spawn: (a) short-circuit on the remembered folder — if `rememberedPullRequestFolder(sessionState, slug)` returns a root, use it and never scan (see MAIN-5); (b) if it does not, do NOT scan on a clipboard event at all — defer the scan until the user actually opens the PR; (c) skip the clipboard read entirely while the app is hidden or has not been used for several minutes, and raise the interval to ~2 s; (d) once MAIN-3's process-level remotes memo exists, a repeat scan costs zero spawns.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes a ~1,300 ms, 103-process background burst from every PR-URL copy; on a matching slug also removes a 3,400-7,000 ms refresh and a network round trip

findings.title: findPullRequestRoot awaits the whole ~/Developer walk before it looks at the remembered checkout it already knows
findings.mechanism: The catalog is only needed for `candidateRoots`. The remembered root (from sessionState.pullRequestFolders, index.ts:517) and the already-open session roots are `preferredRoots` and are probed first inside findMatchingPullRequestRoot (src/main/pullRequestRoots.ts:27-29) — in the overwhelmingly common Cmd+H case the answer is the first preferred root. But line 515 awaits the folder walk unconditionally before any of that runs, so the fast path pays for the slow path. On a cold launch the walk's 90 readdir + 478 stat calls hit a cold FS cache and contend with the renderer boot.
findings.evidence: index.ts:514-527 reads `const catalog = await folderIndex.list(sessionState.approvedRoots)` as the first statement, before `githubRepoSlugFromPullRequestUrl` / `rememberedPullRequestFolder` on 516-517. Warm cost measured at 16.4 ms (103 folders, 90 readdir, 478 stat); the lead measured 45 ms; FolderIndex caches for only 30 s (src/main/folderIndex.ts:29), so a Cmd+H after any idle period always re-walks.
findings.fix: Restructure findPullRequestRoot to try preferred roots first and only then build the catalog: compute `slug`/`remembered` first, call findMatchingPullRequestRoot with `candidateRoots: []`, and if that returns null call `await folderIndex.list(...)` and retry with the full candidate list. Cleanest shape: change the option to `candidateRoots: () => Promise<readonly string[]>` in src/main/pullRequestRoots.ts:11-15 and only invoke it after the preferred and named passes fail. Also raise FolderIndex's CACHE_TTL_MS (folderIndex.ts:29) from 30 s to ~5 min and refresh it in the background rather than on demand.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 16-45 ms (more when cold) off the front of every Cmd+H, and it removes the walk entirely for remembered repositories

findings.title: capWorkspaceCache JSON.stringifies the whole cache on every publish, and above 2 MB enters a `paths.includes()` quadratic halving loop measured at 112 ms
findings.mechanism: workspaceCacheBytes does `new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(cache)).length` — a full serialise of the whole snapshot just to measure it — and capWorkspaceCache calls it once or twice on every invocation. capWorkspaceCache runs from mergeWorkspaceCache (workspaceCache.ts:173) via persistWorkspaceFromSnapshot, which fires from trackSnapshot (index.ts:252-255) on every mutating IPC, from the refresh completion (index.ts:494, 971), from hydrateLastWorkspace (index.ts:950) on the pre-window path, and from the persistWorkspaceUi handler (index.ts:634-639) which the renderer calls on a 250 ms debounce whenever the selected path, view or file text changes (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:955-967). When the cache exceeds MAX_WORKSPACE_CACHE_BYTES the loop at line 97 halves `paths` and re-filters statuses with `paths.includes(entry.path)` — an O(statuses x paths) linear scan inside a filter — re-stringifying the whole cache each iteration.
findings.evidence: Measured with a faithful re-implementation: 3,026 short paths (this machine's actual cache, 198 KB) = 0.3 ms; 20,000 short paths (0.92 MB) = 1.5-2.4 ms; 20,000 realistic deep-monorepo paths (3.57 MB raw, which is what a 20k-path repo actually produces) = 106-112 ms per call, one halving. Also note: the reported '1.9 MB / 20,000 paths' cache does not reproduce here — ~/Library/Application Support/Horus/last-workspace.json is 198,124 bytes with 3,026 paths; readFileSync 0.04 ms and JSON.parse 0.14 ms, so the synchronous pre-window read at index.ts:996 is NOT currently a startup cost. MAX_CACHED_PATHS=20,000 (workspaceCache.ts:4) and MAX_WORKSPACE_CACHE_BYTES=2 MB (line 7) are the caps that make the 112 ms case reachable.
findings.fix: (1) Stop measuring by serialising. Estimate bytes as `snapshot.paths.reduce((n,p)=>n+p.length+3,0) + statuses.length*80 + (fileText?.text.length ?? 0)` and only serialise once, at the actual write in saveWorkspaceCache (src/main/workspaceCacheStore.ts:26). (2) Replace `paths.includes(...)` in the halving loop (line 99) and in parseSelectedPath (line 250) with a Set built once. (3) Cap by path count directly instead of by bytes — pick a fixed MAX_CACHED_PATHS (e.g. 8,000, well under 2 MB for any realistic path length) and delete the loop. (4) Debounce the merge itself, not just the disk write: rememberWorkspaceCache (index.ts:258-266) already has a 400 ms timer, so move mergeWorkspaceCache inside it and keep only the raw snapshot reference until the timer fires.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Up to 112 ms of main-thread block per publish on large repos, at up to 4 publishes/second while the user navigates files

findings.title: A background PR open (activate=false) refreshes the WRONG repository and leaves its own session on stale cached data
findings.mechanism: When the cache matches the requested root, openRepository hydrates it with `activate` (line 489) but then unconditionally calls `repositorySessions.refreshActive()` (line 493), which refreshes whatever root is currently active (src/main/repositorySessions.ts:102-108) — not the root just hydrated. On the Cmd+H path warmupPullRequest calls openRepository(matchingRoot, false) (index.ts:167), so the restored repository is refreshed a SECOND time (another 3.4-7 s ignored walk) while the PR's own repository never gets a live refresh and getPullRequestReview runs against the hydrated cache. The guard on line 494 (`live.root === repositorySessions.activeRoot`) hides the mistake instead of preventing the work.
findings.evidence: index.ts:493 `void repositorySessions.refreshActive()` takes no root argument; src/main/repositorySessions.ts:103 reads `const root = this.#activeRoot`. index.ts:167 passes `activate=false`. The horus:// shim trace shows the restore's refresh running while the warmup path is active.
findings.fix: Add `refresh(root: string)` to RepositorySessionRegistry (mirroring refreshActive but resolving the session by root via `this.#sessions.get(root)`) and call `repositorySessions.refresh(snapshot.root)` at index.ts:493. Keep persistWorkspaceFromSnapshot gated on `live.root === repositorySessions.activeRoot` so a background refresh does not overwrite the restore cache.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes one redundant 3,400-7,000 ms refresh from the Cmd+H path and makes the PR's repository actually current

findings.title: Up to 512 KB of file text crosses IPC every 250 ms and is JSON.stringified twice per crossing
findings.line: 634-639 (persistWorkspaceUi handler); producer at src/renderer/src/App.tsx:955-967; cap at src/shared/workspaceCache.ts:6
findings.mechanism: App.tsx debounces at 250 ms and ships `{selectedPath, workspaceView, fileText}` where fileText.text is the whole current file up to MAX_CACHED_FILE_CHARS = 512 * 1024 characters. Each arrival runs parseWorkspaceUi -> capFileText (a slice) and then persistWorkspaceFromSnapshot -> mergeWorkspaceCache -> capWorkspaceCache, which stringifies the whole cache including that text (MAIN-6), and 400 ms later saveWorkspaceCache stringifies it a third time for the disk write (src/main/workspaceCacheStore.ts:26). While the user scrolls or types in a large file this is a steady structured-clone + serialise load on the main process.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/App.tsx:955-967 `useDebouncedPersist({root, selectedPath, workspaceView, fileText: cachedFileTextFromComparison(...)}, ..., 250)`; src/shared/workspaceCache.ts:6 `MAX_CACHED_FILE_CHARS = 512 * 1024`; workspaceCache.ts:106 stringifies the full cache; src/main/workspaceCacheStore.ts:26 stringifies it again.
findings.fix: Send the file text only when the selected path changes, not on every text edit — the cache exists to paint the last file on next launch, so a slightly stale body is fine. Split the IPC into a cheap `persistWorkspaceUi({selectedPath, workspaceView})` on the 250 ms debounce and a separate `persistWorkspaceFileText` on a 2-3 s debounce that only fires on path change. Lower MAX_CACHED_FILE_CHARS to ~128 KB (a first paint does not need more than a screenful plus scrollback).
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes up to ~1.5 MB/s of IPC + serialise traffic while editing; a few ms per event but continuous

findings.title: No concurrency limit on git spawns: 24 concurrent `git remote -v` observed, each 3-6x slower than it needs to be
findings.mechanism: runCommand is a bare execFile with no queue or semaphore. Concurrency is chosen independently at each call site (REMOTE_PROBE_CONCURRENCY = 8 in src/main/pullRequestRoots.ts:14, MAX_PATCH_COMMAND_CONCURRENCY = 4 in src/main/repository.ts:125, plus the 3 unbounded refresh spawns and the PR pipeline). When three root scans run at once (MAIN-3) that is 24 concurrent forks of git plus a saturating ignored walk, on top of the renderer's boot. maxBuffer is a generous 64 MB (MAX_GIT_OUTPUT_BYTES, gitCommands.ts:4) which is fine, but nothing bounds process count.
findings.evidence: Shim trace of the horus:// cold launch: at 520-530 ms six `remote -v` overlap, by 686-707 ms eight overlap across duplicated roots, and individual probes cost 96-192 ms versus 30 ms measured for the same 103 roots at concurrency 8 on an idle machine (388 ms total, 13 waves, max wave 32 ms).
findings.fix: Add a small global semaphore inside runCommand in src/main/gitCommands.ts — a FIFO of pending starters released as children exit, with a limit of about `Math.max(4, os.availableParallelism() - 2)`. Give it a second, higher-priority lane for interactive calls (getComparison, saveWorkingFile) so a background scan can never starve a keystroke. ~30 lines, and it caps the blast radius of every other finding here.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 3-6x reduction in per-spawn latency whenever more than one subsystem is busy; no change when idle

findings.title: beginSessionRestore runs synchronously inside the whenReady tick, delaying the renderer's first preload sendSync by the hydrate cost
findings.mechanism: createMainWindow calls loadRenderer() and show() but returns before Chromium spawns the renderer. beginSessionRestore then runs on the same tick: hydrateLastWorkspace (index.ts:932-965) does 3 existsSync+realpathSync pairs, a shallow spread of the cached snapshot, `new Set(paths)` and `new Map(statuses)` in #setSnapshot (src/main/repository.ts:2683-2691), fs.watch recursive, and mergeWorkspaceCache -> capWorkspaceCache. At today's 3,026 paths this is ~3 ms and harmless, but capWorkspaceCache alone reaches 112 ms on a 20k-path monorepo (MAIN-6), and the preload's two blocking `ipcRenderer.sendSync` calls (src/preload/index.ts:53-56) cannot be served until the tick ends.
findings.evidence: index.ts:1003-1005 shows createMainWindow(); the applyExternalReview loop; beginSessionRestore() with no await or setImmediate between them. Measured components: fs.watch(recursive) on the 369k-file tree = 0.42 ms; new Set(3,026) + new Map(12) ~0.3 ms; capWorkspaceCache 0.3 ms at 3k paths / 112 ms at 20k long paths.
findings.fix: Wrap the hydrate half in `setImmediate(beginSessionRestore)` so the window-creation tick ends first. Better: split it so `repositorySessions.hydrate(...)` (which the preload's getWorkspaceCache does not need — it reads the module-level `workspaceCache`, index.ts:631) happens after the first yield, while `workspaceCache` and `currentRestoreHint()` stay set synchronously. Also make persistWorkspaceFromSnapshot at index.ts:950 skip the merge entirely on the restore path — it is re-persisting data just read off disk unchanged.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0-115 ms off preload unblock, scaling with repo size

findings.title: The preload blocks twice on sendSync and re-validates the whole cache (including a JSON.stringify) before any renderer script runs
findings.mechanism: `restoreHintFromArgv(process.argv) ?? parseRestoreHint(ipcRenderer.sendSync(getRestoreHint))` then `parseWorkspaceCache(ipcRenderer.sendSync(getWorkspaceCache))`. The second ships the entire cache object across the process boundary synchronously and then re-validates it with parseWorkspaceCache -> parseCachedSnapshot + parseStatuses (builds a Set of paths) + capWorkspaceCache (another full JSON.stringify, MAIN-6). Main already validated the same bytes at index.ts:996. The first sendSync is usually avoided because encodeRestoreHintArgument puts the hint in additionalArguments (index.ts:330), but currentRestoreHint() is still recomputed — with two more existsSync+realpathSync calls — inside each sync handler (index.ts:628-632).
findings.evidence: src/preload/index.ts:53-56; src/main/index.ts:628-632 both handlers call currentRestoreHint(); currentRestoreHint (index.ts:597) calls resolveExistingRoot which does existsSync + realpathSync (src/main/workspaceListing.ts:23-28). At 198 KB this is sub-millisecond; at the 2 MB cap it is a multi-millisecond synchronous cross-process hop plus a 112 ms cap pass.
findings.fix: Compute currentRestoreHint() once per launch and memoise it (invalidate on setStartupPreferences / rememberOpenedRoot). Trust the cache main already parsed: send it as a plain object and skip parseWorkspaceCache in the preload, or add a `parseWorkspaceCacheTrusted` that does the shape checks without capWorkspaceCache. Better still, hand the cache to the renderer over the async channel it already has and let the first paint use only the restore hint (tiny, already in argv), so nothing blocks preload at all.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 1-5 ms today, up to ~120 ms on a large repo, on the strict critical path before any renderer JS

findings.title: The boot CSS preload is discarded by Chromium: `rel=preload as=style` is emitted without crossorigin, so the stylesheet is fetched twice
findings.line: 154 (`attrs: { rel: 'preload', as: 'style', href: ... }` in preloadBootChunkPlugin); the JS branch on 148 correctly sets crossorigin
findings.mechanism: The JS chunk gets `{ rel: 'modulepreload', crossorigin: '' }` but the CSS gets no crossorigin, so its credentials mode does not match the later stylesheet request and Chromium drops the preloaded response. The preload is pure waste and the 172 KB boot CSS is requested a second time on the render-blocking path.
findings.evidence: Captured from the installed app's own console on a clean launch (ELECTRON_ENABLE_LOGGING=1): "A preload for '.../assets/boot-B2Joa_jX.css' is found, but is not used because the request credentials mode does not match. Consider taking a look at crossorigin attribute." followed by "...boot-B2Joa_jX.css was preloaded using link preload but not used within a few seconds from the window's load event."
findings.fix: Add `crossorigin: ''` to the CSS branch at electron.vite.config.ts:154 so it matches the modulepreload branch on line 148. Given the boot CSS is 172 KB and render-blocking, also consider inlining it into index.html instead of preloading it at all.
findings.estimatedGainMs: One duplicate 172 KB file:// fetch on the render-blocking path, roughly 20-60 ms of first-paint

findings.title: Opening a new folder paints a 400-path placeholder that now sits for seconds before jumping to the real tree
findings.line: 5 (MAX_LISTING_PATHS = 400) and 43-77 (listRootSnapshot); consumed at src/main/repository.ts:1322 and src/main/repositorySessions.ts:120,152
findings.mechanism: repositorySessions.open returns a synchronous two-level readdir capped at 400 paths and fires the real refresh with `void` (repositorySessions.ts:152). The IPC therefore answers in ~60-100 ms (realpath + `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` + the readdir) — genuinely instant — but the explorer then shows a truncated, alphabetically-clipped tree until the refresh lands. Before e18053e that gap was ~60 ms and invisible; with MAIN-1 it is 3.4-7 s, and the arriving snapshot carries a brand-new `paths` array so the whole explorer re-renders. That mismatch, not the dialog, is what makes 'open a new folder' feel like it regressed.
findings.evidence: workspaceListing.ts:5 `const MAX_LISTING_PATHS = 400`; repositorySessions.ts:152 `void this.#refreshAndPublish({ repository, watcher })` immediately before `return snapshot` on 153; #refreshAndPublish (repositorySessions.ts:191-206) computes changedPaths with `new Set(['*'])` on a null previous, i.e. every status path. Shim-measured refresh cost on the two large repos: 3.4-7.1 s.
findings.fix: MAIN-1 alone closes the gap to ~130 ms and makes this invisible. Additionally: publish the tracked+status snapshot as soon as those two fast spawns resolve (MAIN-1's secondary hardening) so the placeholder is replaced in ~60 ms and the ignored set arrives later as an additive update; and mark placeholder snapshots (`partial: true`) so the explorer can render a loading affordance instead of a tree that silently changes shape.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 3,400-7,000 ms of visibly-wrong tree after every folder open

findings.title: The startup benchmark cannot pass: it waits for a review surface that a plain restore never renders
findings.mechanism: sampleStartup requires BOTH `#repository-explorer` AND `.multi-file-review, .multi-file-code-view` within 6 s, then throws 'The restored explorer and review surface did not become usable.' On a restore of materialsx-core-3 (12 statuses) the explorer appears at 544 ms but no multi-file review surface is ever mounted, so the loop always times out. The benchmark's failure was read as 'startup > 6 s'; it is actually a stale selector, and the real numbers are far better than the failure implied.
findings.evidence: Direct CDP probe of the same installed build: `#repository-explorer` present at 544 ms; `.multi-file-review, .multi-file-code-view` still absent after 12 s of polling, while document.body.innerText reads 'materialsx-core-3 | 411 MB | dev | 3,026 files'. mainStartupMetrics from the same run: appReady 74.7, windowCreated 136.2, windowShown 146.3, restoreSettled 3,615.7.
findings.fix: Split the benchmark's gates: report explorerUsableMs from `#repository-explorer` alone and make the review gate optional (or point it at whatever root element the multi-file view emits today). Add restoreSettled from `window.repository.getPerformanceMetrics(true)` as a first-class metric, since that is the number MAIN-1 moves. Raise HORUS_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS above the current restore time so a regression shows as a slow number rather than a thrown error.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 (measurement correctness, not runtime) — but without it no one can see MAIN-1's 3.4 s

findings.title: resolveExistingRoot / rootsMatch do repeated synchronous existsSync+realpathSync on the pre-window path
findings.mechanism: Every rootsMatch is two resolveExistingRoot calls and each of those is an existsSync plus a realpathSync. currentRestoreHint (index.ts:597) does one, and it runs from createMainWindow's additionalArguments (index.ts:330) and from both sendSync handlers (index.ts:628-632). openRepository does one plus a rootsMatch (index.ts:478-481); hydrateLastWorkspace another two (index.ts:936, 941) plus detectRepositoryKind (another existsSync). On a warm APFS cache this is tens of microseconds each and does not currently matter, but they are all on the strictly synchronous pre-window path and will matter over a network mount.
findings.evidence: workspaceListing.ts:21-28 `existsSync(root)` then `realpathSync(root)`; workspaceListing.ts:30-35 rootsMatch calls it twice; the call sites listed above run before or during createMainWindow.
findings.fix: Memoise resolved roots in a Map for the lifetime of the process (invalidated on openRepository and on any 'folder no longer on disk' error). Replace the existsSync+realpathSync pair with a single realpathSync in a try/catch — realpathSync already fails for a missing path, so the existsSync is a redundant syscall.
findings.estimatedGainMs: <1 ms locally; removes ~12 redundant syscalls from the pre-window path and protects against network-mounted roots

openQuestions: The '1.9 MB / 20,000-path last-workspace.json' in the brief does not reproduce: the file on this machine is 198,124 bytes with 3,026 paths and parses in 0.14 ms, so the synchronous pre-window read is not currently a cost. Was that measured on a different repository (the caps are MAX_CACHED_PATHS=20,000 and MAX_WORKSPACE_CACHE_BYTES=2 MB), or before a cap was added? MAIN-6's 112 ms halving loop only fires above 2 MB, so knowing whether the user actually reaches that size decides its severity.

Two probe runs disagreed on restoreSettled (264 ms vs 3,616 ms). The 264 ms run had ~/Developer/vibes/imux as lastRoot (a repo where the ignored walk costs 126 ms); the 3,616 ms run had materialsx-core-3. Worth confirming with the user that materialsx-core-3 is the repo they launch into, since MAIN-1's impact scales entirely with the ignored-file count (369,122 there vs a few thousand in imux).

The refresh self-retrigger (MAIN-2) settled after exactly 3 cycles in my test. I did not determine whether a longer-running external writer (a dev server, a python venv, a build) keeps it going indefinitely. Watching a git-spawn log during `bun dev` in materialsx-core-3 would settle it, and would say whether MAIN-2 is 11 s per save or continuous.

The recursive fs.watch covers node_modules/.venv/dist (369k ignored files). It cost 0.42 ms to construct and produced zero events in 1.5 s idle, so it is not a startup cost — but I did not measure the event rate during an `npm install` or a build, where FSEvents would deliver tens of thousands of paths into normalizeChangedPath on the main thread. If that is measurable, the watch should be scoped or excluded segments filtered before they reach JS.

I did not exercise a real GitHub PR fetch (needs network + gh auth, and belongs to the PR-path agent). The 307-spawn horus:// trace used a deliberately non-matching slug, so it measures the root-scan cost only; the matching case additionally opens a repository (another MAIN-1 walk) and runs the gh pipeline. Total Cmd+H time will be dominated by whichever of those is slower once MAIN-1 and MAIN-3 are fixed.

Whether `--no-optional-locks` is safe for every status call here: it also suppresses the index refresh that makes subsequent `git diff` calls fast. Worth checking whether getComparison / getWorkingTreePatch get slower when the index is never refreshed, or whether an explicit `git update-index --refresh` on an idle timer is the better shape.
